description: Tombs of Terror bosses D (phase 8 family 22): eighteen encounters of Saviors of Uldum's Tombs of Terror (ULDA_BOSS_60 to ULDA_BOSS_79 without 64 and 67: Zaraam, Kyriss, A Beautiful Oasis, Vessina, Thrud, Siamat, Weaponized Wasp, Isiset, Rajh, Ammunae, Setesh, General Husam, High Prophet Barim, Avozu, Tarkus, Gorebite, Octosari, Armadillobot) and Siamat's Servant (ULDA_026). Boss deck lists are transcribed from hearthstone.wiki.gg boss pages (read 2026-11-14), by card name; tools/dungeon-run-catalog (step 'encounters') resolves the names against facts/violet-hold-2026-09.json, checks every card and writes data/dungeon-run/encounters-v1.json. Every Tombs boss hero prints 10 Health (A Beautiful Oasis 30): Health is the act curve's, and the tier is the boss's level band read from its page's deck table (levels 1-2: tier 1; 2-3 and 3-4: tier 2; 5-6: tier 3; 7: tier 4; family 19's verify/tools/gen/p8f19/tombs_tiers.py).
method: The wiki's MediaWiki API was read for each page twice: the wikitext (action=raw) and the rendered deck table (action=parse, rowspans and colspans expanded); the two agree. Each Normal table is transcribed in table order with its own counts (25 or 30 cards); a table of possible cards without counts ("10; 15", "15; 20", Gorebite's) is transcribed with count null. Where the Normal list is shorter than 30 the Heroic table is transcribed too and is the row's extend list. A page's level note ("These decks correspond only to level N") and its chapter line are recorded in the row's schedule adaptation. The file is written by verify/tools/gen/p8f22/make_f22.py.

adaptations.note: Tombs boss heroes print 10 Health (the adventure set a boss's Health by level server-side): the fight's Health is the act curve's and the tier is the boss's level in its chapter, from its wiki page's deck table: level 7 (a full 30-card list with no smaller lower-level version, the shape of a chapter's seventh boss, the last before its Plague Lord) = tier 4. The page names chapter 3 as the chapter the boss is first met in (after it, any completed chapter), which does not set its level.

Forbidden Power (4) deals N damage to a random enemy character (the run player's hero or a minion an effect can pick, game RNG); N is the power's own script number (the @ of its text), 1 at the start and +1 whenever a minion of the boss's dies (a public death), so the client shows the current value. The hero power damage rules apply to the hit.
The page's trivia names Zaraam a seventh-floor encounter, which matches the level-7 shape of its full 30-card list.

Chain Lightning (4) deals 1 damage to a minion (any minion; the hero power damage rules apply to each hit); while the minion it hit last survives, it jumps to a minion adjacent to it on its board (a random one of the two neighbours, game RNG; a dormant or permanent minion is no neighbour) and hits again, until one dies or no neighbour is left. A hit that does nothing (an Immune minion) ends the chain.

The wiki's list is the level 6 deck; on level 5 the original removes 5 random cards. Here the row always uses the level 6 list.

Mirage (0), auto-cast as the page states (DungeonRunEncounters.TombsD: at the start of the boss's turn while the run player's hand holds a card and has room): it gives the run player an illusion card, a copy of a random card of the run player's own hand (game RNG); one of the two (the original or the copy, game RNG) is the illusion. The client data has no illusion token (the power's text names none, the page names none), so the illusion is that copy, as the page's notes describe: "Mirage creates a copy of a random card in the player's hand (illusion). This effect lasts until the end of the player's turn"; "only one random copy of the illusion discards a card. The other copy can be played as a normal card"; "the illusion can discard its second copy". Played, the illusion resolves as its card and its player discards a random card of the hand (the second copy too, if chosen). At the end of the run player's turn the illusion leaves the hand if it is still there; when both are still there the copy leaves and the original stays, so the hand is as before ("if the player does not play any of the two copies ... none of the player's cards will be discarded"). Which card is the illusion is kept in private encounter tags; the boss never learns the copied card (a hidden card of the run player's hand).

Plaguebringer (passive): the spells in the boss's hand cost (2) less (a hand aura), and each spell the boss plays (not countered) Overloads it by (1) more, on top of its own Overload, so Tunnel Trogg, Thunderhead's and Eternal Sentinel's Overload rules see it. Spells cast by an effect are not played and do not Overload.

Ogre-Sized Thief (3) takes a random card of the run player's deck (game RNG) into the boss's hand: the deck-steal rule of the boss shrine TRLA_186 (DungeonRunShrines.TakeFromDeck: a deck exit and a transfer whose definition only the new owner sees). The boss learns exactly the card it took and nothing else; the run player sees a card leave its deck. A full hand burns it. Offered while the run player's deck, whose count is public, holds a card.
